samples.summary: API insert/delete (`applyWorksheetShift`) still does not snap the freeze past a straddling merge, so the v1 API is not actually held to the invariant the change documents
samples.evidence: `Sheet.shiftCells` now runs `snapFreezePastMerges` after the boundary adjustment (sheet.ts:1418-1429), and docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:129-136 asserts "The v1 worksheet API is held to the same invariant, since it is the other writer of these fields". But `applyWorksheetShift` — the helper the v1 `POST .../rows|columns` insert/delete endpoints use, whose comment says "Mirrors `Sheet.shiftCells`" (line 246-248) — only grows/shrinks `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` and never snaps. An insert or delete through the API can therefore still leave a merged block straddling the freeze, the exact non-drawable state the change exists to prevent, while `move`, `freeze` and `merges` refuse/snap. The shared `snapFreezePastMerges` helper is already exported from `@wafflebase/sheets` and would have closed the gap.

samples.summary: REST API design doc (and cli.md) not updated for the new 409s and the snapping freeze response
samples.evidence: rest-api.md:314 still reads "**A move that would split a merged range returns `409`.**" with no mention of the new freeze-straddle refusal; nothing in rest-api.md documents that `PUT .../freeze` may now answer with a *different* boundary than requested, or that `PUT .../merges` can 409. docs/design/cli.md:1607/1620-1625 carries the same per-command contract table (`sheets.move` → "409 if it would split a merged range", `sheets.freeze.set`, `sheets.merges.set`) and is likewise untouched. The behavior is described only in docs/design/sheets/sheet.md, i.e. the canonical API docs now disagree with the shipped contract.

samples.summary: ~90 lines of freeze/copy-buffer/REST-API design folded into a single paste bullet instead of the sections that own those topics
samples.evidence: The whole new narrative (freeze snapping, `shiftCells` snap, v1 API rules, copy-buffer lifetime and axis-ID revalidation, `moveRows` returning a boolean) is appended under the "Clipboard/paste" bullet, while the doc already has a "Freeze Panes" section (line 582-611, whose "Insert/delete near boundary" paragraph is now incomplete) and a "Merged Cell Model" section whose line 322 still flatly says "Merges that cross freeze pane boundaries are disallowed" without mentioning the snapping behavior. The canonical sections are left stale while the new rules live somewhere a reader of the freeze section will not find them.

samples.summary: `rangeOf` spread-to-fold rewrite plus a 200k-cell test is an unrelated performance fix ridden along with the merge/paste work
samples.evidence: The `rangeOf` change (and its stack-overflow test in test/sheet/coordinates.test.ts) is a separate defect from the merge-paste/freeze feature; it is only touched here because `selectPastedRange` was refactored to call it. Harmless, but it widens the change's surface beyond the stated subject.

finding.summary: API insert/delete (`applyWorksheetShift`) still does not snap the freeze past a straddling merge, so the v1 API is not actually held to the invariant the change documents
finding.evidence: `Sheet.shiftCells` now runs `snapFreezePastMerges` after the boundary adjustment (sheet.ts:1418-1429), and docs/design/sheets/sheet.md:129-136 asserts "The v1 worksheet API is held to the same invariant, since it is the other writer of these fields". But `applyWorksheetShift` — the helper the v1 `POST .../rows|columns` insert/delete endpoints use, whose comment says "Mirrors `Sheet.shiftCells`" (line 246-248) — only grows/shrinks `frozenRows`/`frozenCols` and never snaps. An insert or delete through the API can therefore still leave a merged block straddling the freeze, the exact non-drawable state the change exists to prevent, while `move`, `freeze` and `merges` refuse/snap. The shared `snapFreezePastMerges` helper is already exported from `@wafflebase/sheets` and would have closed the gap.

verdict.reason: The absence is factually real — `applyWorksheetShift` (worksheet-structure.ts:515-595 via shiftWorksheetViewState:246-265) only grows/shrinks frozenRows/frozenCols, and the v1 insert/delete controller path (worksheet-structure.controller.ts:322-367) adds no snap — but it is not blocking under this lens. A shift cannot CREATE a straddling block: shiftMergeAxis (merging.ts:31-60) and the freeze adjustment move the merge and the boundary by matching amounts in every branch (insert inside the band grows both by `count`; a delete reaching past the band leaves the boundary at i-1 while the surviving fragment starts at i). The repo's own test confirms this — merge.test.ts:833-845 must seed the straddle directly through MemStore because "A block already across the boundary is a state this replica cannot create", making the shiftCells snap a healer for import/peer-written state, not a guard. The design doc's API sentence (sheet.md:130-137) enumerates precisely the three endpoints that can write a straddle (move/freeze/merges), all of which are guarded in the backend (worksheet.controller.ts:112-119, 240-247; worksheet-structure.controller.ts:173-196); it does not assert that insert/delete snaps. So no acceptance criterion is left unmet for a user: an API insert/delete leaves an already non-drawable imported document exactly as broken as it was before the call. The cost is confined to a missed reuse of an available helper (an unhealed import), which is `minor` under this rubric and does not block.
